idea: Italian agricultural land sourcing and investment analysis for UK buyers
buyer: UK and international HNW buyers of Italian farmland
pain: Buying Italian land is opaque, and the numbers are never analysed properly
v1: Source and analyse three estates for one buyer
verdict: Genuine access nobody else has, paired with financial rigour buyers never get - but the client flow is tiny.

why.distribution: Her husband's Italian agriculture contacts give supply-side access; buyers must be found separately.
why.demand: Buying agents for Italian estates exist and are paid, usually without any financial analysis.
why.fmf: Investment analysis plus a property eye plus genuine local access; she is not an agricultural specialist.
why.revenue_structure: One mandate per buyer, rarely repeating.
why.defensibility: Local access plus institutional analytical rigour is a genuinely unique pairing in this market.
why.tailwind: Farmland as an asset class is slowly institutionalising.
why.ceiling: £22k x 9 mandates = £198k, and nine Italian farmland purchases a year is far beyond plausible flow.

ceiling_arithmetic: £22k x 9 mandates = £198k less ~20% costs = £158k. Realistic buyer flow through personal introductions is 1-3 a year = £18-53k.
carries: The most defensible position in the set - local access plus analytical rigour that literally nobody else in this market combines.
kills: Buyer flow. Italian farmland purchases by analysable UK buyers happen a handful of times a year.
test: Ask her husband's contacts whether two estates are quietly for sale, and separately find one interested buyer.
test_pass: A buyer engages for a paid search.
test_fail: Plenty of estates, no buyers - the likely asymmetry.
